reasoning_traces.think:
Homogeneous grouping transforms individual uncertainty into statistical regularity, enabling prediction. However, the"paradox"arises because perfect classification is impossible; each subgroup introduces new sources of dependence. Non-hereditary independence means that even if individual trials were independent, repeated grouping creates temporal or contextual coupling. These primitives formalize how aggregation induces structure: hierarchical Bayesian models capture hereditary properties, while conformal methods preserve marginal coverage under exchangeability. The failure mode occurs when overfitting causes groups to lose representativeness, leading to systematic miscalibration.
